articles.title: India: Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' released
articles.summary: The book goes through the Italian-born matriarch's journey with one of India's most politically influential families. It has already garnered political controversy, with the ruling BJP accusing her…

image.caption: Sonia Gandhi has said that her memoir is not a 'political book' but a 'personal' one [FILE: Jun 4, 2024]Image: Sondeep Shankar/Pacific Press/picture alliance

blocks.text: A memoir bysenior Congress leader and former party president Sonia Gandhi went on sale on Tuesday, with its pages offering a rare insight by the private politician into how she came from humble Italian origins and went on to become the matriarch of India's most powerful political dynasty — the Nehru-Gandhi family.
The book called "Belonging: A Journey of Love" has been published by HarperCollins India.

"Much has been written about my family, but rarely with real insight into who they were, their motivations, their struggles, their very human flaws. I wanted to portray them honestly, as people I knew and loved," 79-year-old Gandhi wrote in The Hindu daily newspaper earlier this week.
Who is Sonia Gandhi?

Born Sonia Maino in 1946 in a small Italian village near Vicenza, she met Rajiv Gandhi — the grandson of India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru — at a restaurant in the United Kingdom's Cambridge city.
The two got married in New Delhi in 1968, when Rajiv's mother and Nehru's daughter Indira Gandhi was serving as India's prime minister.

Nearly two decades later, Sonia would find herself holding her bloodied and dying mother-in-law in her arms following a 1984 assassination that saw Indira's bodyguards shoot her to avenge her suppression of an insurgency that culminated in an army assault, called Operation Blue Star, on the holiest Sikh shrine, the Golden Temple.
Sonia's husband Rajiv Gandhi, a pilot who was propelled into politics after his mother's death, became India's youngest prime minister at 40 years old.
He too was assassinated in a suicide bombing in 1991.
Sonia Gandhi later entered politics, going on to become the longest-serving president of the Congress party.
India's Congress Party hopes to make comeback
Sonia Gandhi's book sheds light on India's politically influential Nehru-Gandhi family
The Nehru-Gandhi family gave India three prime ministers. In her book Sonia Gandhi talks about her 2004 decision to not take up the top job as prime minister of the world's largest democracy.

In an excerpt from her book, published in The Indian Express, Sonia said her children — and now senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi — had then discussed with her, their mother's possible prime ministership.
"One of them asked me straight out whether I would accept the post, just in case our party pulled off a victory. 'Absolutely not' I'd said, almost indignantly,' the excerpt read.

"Neither Rahul nor Priyanka felt that I should become prime minister. They'd lived through the trauma of their grandmother's assassination and the brutal murder of their father. In their minds, holding that office was intrinsically linked with heightened danger. They looked relieved and I, too, felt lighter, having said my views out loud on the question for the first time," Sonia writes.
Ruling BJP accuses Sonia Gandhi of 'whitewashing'
Sonia Gandhi has said that her memoir is not a "political book" but a "personal" one.
But with the Tuesday launch, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of Prime Minister Narendra Modi attacked the Congress veteran.

BJP National spokesperson C R Kesavan said that Sonia Gandhi should have named her book "whitewashing" as he accused the memoir of "sugar coating the historical wrongs perpetrated by the Nehru-Gandhi family."

The book has also been released at a time when the Congress party looks to regain ground against the BJP, with Sonia's son Rahul Gandhi rallying India's opposition parties in a series of protests over the last month.

articles.title: Both sides in VP Sara impeachment trial flag possible violations of sub judice rule
articles.summary: The defense on Tuesday raised concerns about the prosecution"s possible violation of the sub judice rule, but the latter countered saying that Vice President Duterte herself may have also disregarded…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 7:42pm

The defense on Tuesday raised concerns about the prosecution’s possible violation of the sub judice rule, but the latter countered saying that Vice President Duterte herself may have also disregarded the rule with her “incessant attacks” against the integrity of the impeachment court.

This developed on Day 41 of the impeachment trial, as defense lead counsel Sheila Sison said they will be submitting to the clerk of court a copy of the link containing the alleged sub judice statements made by certain private prosecutors.

“These statements not only go into a fair comment. In fact, they go into the probative value of their supposed cross examination and of the weight of the evidence presented by the defense yesterday and of the testimonial weight given by the witnesses,” she said.
Sison said she is pertaining to a press conference conducted by the prosecution on Monday and the statements made by private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr.
In response, Tolosa said the prosecution also reserves the right to file corresponding motions for declaration of violation of subjudice rule supposedly made by the Vice President herself.
“I think it does not escape everyone, the incessant attacks against the integrity of the impeachment court itself and the senator-judges by no less than the Vice President,” he said.

The Senate impeachment court earlier issued a ruling barring senator-judges, as well as counsels of both the prosecution and the defense, from speaking on the merits of the impeachment case against Duterte.

In a recent ruling, the impeachment court ruled that the sub judice principle under Rule 18 of the Rules of Procedure on impeachment trials shall apply “with equal force” to all articles of impeachment, whether withdrawn or pending adjudication.

The House prosecution panel earlier dropped three out of the four Articles of Impeachment leveled against the Vice President, saying its case would stand on Article II alone on alleged unexplained wealth due to non-full declaration of assets and non-divestment of business.

The withdrawn impeachment articles were: Article I on confidential funds, Article III on bribery, and Article IV on assassination plot, grave threats, and inciting to sedition against President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold news briefing as he faces possible impeachment – US politics live
articles.summary: Anti-Trump Republican Thomas Massie pursuing measures against defense secretary as Iran war blamed for party’s sweeping midterm losses

blocks.text: Key events

items: 38m agoHegseth to hold first news briefing since May as he faces possible impeachment

blocks.text: Majorities of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress to act to end the war with Iran and to repeal tariffs put in place by president Donald Trump, signalling demand for quick action to address ⁠the high cost of living, ⁠a new Reuters/Ipsos poll found.

The ​four-day poll, completed on Monday, showed 71% of Americans – including 93% of Democrats and 51% of Republicans – want US Congress to pass legislation ending the conflict with Iran that Trump launched alongside US ally Israel in ⁠February.

Democrats won their largest majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives since at least 2008 in last week’s midterm elections, in a sharp rebuke to Trump’s Republicans over high costs and a deeply unpopular war. Democrats will take power when the new Congress ⁠is sworn in on 3 January.

On their first day back in the Capitol after comprehensive defeats in last week’s midterm elections, Republicans were divided into two camps: those who saw the catastrophe coming, and those who did not.

“I told you exactly what was going to happen. Over and over and over, I told you,” said West Virginia senator Jim Justice. “I said really and truly, if you weren’t concerned and you were a Republican, you were living in a cave. That was my exact words.”
“No one anticipated the magnitude,” said congressman Warren Davidson of Ohio. “I mean, you can’t tell me that the guy that ran as a Democrat for senator in Mississippi thought he was going to win.”

While Scott Colom hasn’t officially been declared the winner in Mississippi’s knife-edge US Senate race – a state that has not sent a Democratic to the chamber since 1982 – there was indeed plenty of evidence before the Tuesday vote that Republicans were in for it.

Not only does the party in power historically suffer defeats in midterm elections, but Donald Trump’s approval ratings had cratered with voters, even on issues that he had previously polled well on, while Democrats had surged in both special and off-year elections.

Nonetheless, few pollsters or political analysts were publicly forecasting the 54-seat Senate majority and 254-seat House majority Democrats won – both of which may expand even further as ballot counting continues.

“People are mad, and they have a right to be mad. They’re disappointed, and they feel like we haven’t delivered, and we deserve exactly what we got,” said Senator John Curtis of Utah. His state is deeply red, but last Tuesday Democrats managed to break the Republican supermajority in the state house of representatives by gaining at least 14 seats – a feat repeated in legislatures across the country.
Hegseth to hold first news briefing since May as he faces possible impeachment
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Defense secretary Pete Hegseth is set to hold a rare news conference later today as he pushes back against congressional efforts to remove him from office for alleged misconduct.

Under pressure after President Donald Trump and Vice-president JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections, Hegseth now faces impeachment proceedings in the House of Representatives.

“There’s a lot of politically motivated people who... may have substantial policy disagreements but their disagreements are with success,” Hegseth told reporters on Monday when asked about efforts to remove him.

“I couldn’t be more proud of what our president has done, the decisions that he’s made, the courageous calls that he’s made, the bold nature of our... military leadership, the skill and courage of the troops on the ground,” he said.

The impeachment efforts are being spearheaded by representative Thomas Massie, an anti-Trump Republican lawmaker who is leaving office after losing a primary contest to a candidate backed by the president, AFP reported.

Several of the articles of impeachment – which Massie introduced on Monday – relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on and oversight of US military interventions.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Massie accused Hegseth of using “our troops to go seize oil for large corporations in America” and derided the Trump administration’s refusal to acknowledge the bombing of a school in Iran.

“I mean, obviously we hit it, and you can determine what kind of missiles from the range and the kind of destruction there was. I don’t think they’re going to get out of that article of impeachment by saying, ‘oh, we don’t know who bombed that school’ – although I think the president tried that for a day or two,” Massie said.
It comes as the president said that the war in Iran is “effectively over” as he played down concerns that the US would escalate its military campaign against Tehran after the midterm elections.
During a White House press conference, Trump said that Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.
In other developments:

items: Donald Trump was joined by Dana White, the CEO of UFC, at a press conference. At the conference, Trump defended Hegseth, saying his defense secretary “won two wars”, and called Massie “a stone cold loser” and “sick”.

After saying that his deportation policy was “too tough” and offering to strike an immigration deal with Democrats in an interview on 60 Minutes broadcast on Sunday, Donald Trump on Monday said his administration’s deportation policy was “very strong.” “Somebody suggested, will there be amnesty? No, but— they came in. They knew the law,” Trump told reporters during a press conference today. He added that he had not spoken with incoming chief of staff Stephen Miller about any changes.

In its first major move since last week’s elections, the Senate has advanced bipartisan legislation to speed up permitting reviews for data centers and other infrastructure projects. The Senate voted 73-25 to formally take up the bill, which would shorten the timeline for approving both clean and fossil fuel energy projects.

A Utah judge scheduled the trial of the man accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk for June 2028. District Judge Tony Graf allocated 105 days for the trial. Graf said the 2028 date balances the defense’s right to prepare with the Kirk family’s desire for a speedy resolution.

The Supreme Court will allow the Trump administration to resume border wall construction in the Big Bend region of Texas. The majority paused a lower court’s decision as the case plays out. The Trump administration had filed an emergency appeal, saying there are illegal border crossings and drug seizures in the region.

After initially saying he would accept the results of the midterm elections, Trump has begun to cast doubt Democrats’ electoral wins. “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” he wrote on Truth Social. Democratic senator Chuck Schumer responded to Trump’s statement, saying that the president’s “return to election denialism was inevitable”.

articles.title: Oil price relief as Trump declares US war on Iran ‘ending fairly soon’ | First Thing
articles.summary:
Speaking in the White House, the president said the US remained ‘locked and loaded’ but escalation was not needed. Plus how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus

Good morning. Oil…

blocks.text: Good morning. Oil prices have dropped after Donald Trump unilaterally declared that the US war on Iran was “effectively over”. During a White House press conference, Trump said Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.

He said, however, that the US remained “locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason”, adding: “We’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.” Brent crude has dropped below $90, its lowest level since August.

items: What is the latest development with Pete Hegseth? A Republican lawmaker has moved to force a vote to impeach the US defense secretary. Thomas Massie, of Kentucky, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, accusing him of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers.

What has happened at a US airbase in England? The US military has reportedly evacuated aircraft from a second airbase in ⁠Britain after a threat from Iran. Two US refuelling tankers that were using the RAF Mildenhall military base diverted to Germany on Monday morning, while several other tankers at the base ⁠were moved to Germany and other locations later in the day.

blocks.caption: Jensen Huang. Photograph: Jeffrey McWhorter/AP

blocks.text: Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, have been accused of defrauding shareholders in a lawsuit over the Chinese spying scandal engulfing the $4.3tn company. The legal action came as Donald Trump said the FBI was investigating Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

There is little public information available about Alice Huang, a fact that has only added fuel to claims she is an intelligence asset. Rebecca Bailey has put together what we know about her, while Aisha Down and Dan Milmo have this exploration of how the affair may have harmed US security.
US supreme court allows construction of Trump’s border wall in Texas’s Big Bend to resume

blocks.caption: A portion of border wall under construction. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: The US supreme court has allowed Donald Trump to continue his administration’s construction of a border wall in Texas’s Big Bend region, including parts of Big Bend national park. The nation’s highest court granted the Trump administration’s emergency request to suspend a lower court order that had temporarily stopped the project.
Opponents have argued the project threatens wildlife and public lands, and could destroy “iconic sections” of the Rio Grande’s protected river corridor.
Judge clears way for Lindsay Clancy to be retried on murder charges

blocks.caption: Lindsay Clancy. Photograph: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger/Reuters

blocks.text: A Massachusetts judge cleared the way for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on ⁠murder charges for killing her three young children, saying a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject her to a ⁠double prosecution for the same ⁠crime. He rejected an attempt by Clancy’s attorneys to have the case against her dismissed.
In September the judge declared ⁠a mistrial after the jury reported that a holdout juror was preventing it from reaching a unanimous verdict. March has been floated as the timing for a second trial.
Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault

blocks.caption: Court artist drawing of Brand in the dock at Southwark crown court, London, as he is sentenced. Photograph: Elizabeth Cook/PA

blocks.text: The disgraced actor and comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced in London to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault.

Brand – who has recently tried to reinvent himself as a Christian influencer and has been a featured speaker for a Maha group allied with RFK Jr – was described by the British judge as a sexual predator who had used his fame and power to carry out crimes and protect himself.
In other news …

blocks.caption: Winner of the Booker prize M John Harrison. Photograph: WIktor Szymanowicz/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

items: M John Harrison has won the Booker prize for The End of Everything, a post-apocalyptic novel set on a near-future Kent coast in England. The 81-year-old becomes the oldest winner in the award’s history, and the first science fiction author to win it.
France has said Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were behind “unprecedented” cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month.
An Ohio State fraternity has been suspended after a viral video showed two men on fire. The university and police are conducting investigations over the “extremely concerning incident”.
California voters failed to pass a proposed one-time tax on billionaires’ wealth.
Joe Biden will undertake only limited promotion of his upcoming White House memoir because of advancing cancer, the former president has said.
Boeing will cut about 5% of its commercial plane workforce through a mix of layoffs and attrition.
Hungarian authorities have detained the brother of Viktor Orbán as part of a people-smuggling ⁠investigation.
The only known handwritten final draft of MLK Jr’s I Have a Dream speech is to be auctioned. The document is expected to fetch more than $10m and the proceeds will be donated to several charities.

blocks.text: Stat of the day: More than 400,000 Russians killed fighting in Ukraine war, leaked data suggests

blocks.caption: Russian president Vladimir Putin. Photograph: Alexander Kazakov/Sputnik/Kremlin pool/EPA

blocks.text: Death records leaked from the state statistics agency, Rosstat, have revealed losses since Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began that are unprecedented in Russia’s modern history. The news comes as talks begin in Abu Dhabi, with US officials seeking a “final end” to the war and a new “long-term security architecture” between Moscow and Europe.
Culture pick: Amazon’s sturdy Muhammad Ali series is a tale told too many times

blocks.caption: A still from The Greatest. Photograph: Brooke Palmer/Prime

blocks.text: There are small pleasures to be had in The Greatest, but this straightforward retelling of the boxing champ’s life doesn’t have much most viewers haven’t seen before, Andrew Lawrence says. But at least it isn’t All’s Fair. Lucy Mangan gave season one zero stars. Season two has earned one. “Is this getting good?” she asks. No, I suspect is the answer.
Don’t miss this: How Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus

blocks.caption: Grand Theft Auto 6 will arrive next week. Photograph: Rockstar Games

blocks.text: I’ve already devoted five minutes to clearing out the storage on my PS5 in anticipation of the mammoth download dropping. Christian Donlan explores the phenomenon that is GTA, with the newest instalment set to arrive next week.
Climate check: Slight fall in carbon emissions from fossil fuels as Iran war drives renewables push

blocks.caption: Flare stack at a petroleum refinery in Texas. Photograph: Rex Wholster/Alamy

blocks.text: Soaring oil and gas prices following the war in Iran have encouraged people to look beyond fossil fuels, leading to an easing of climate-damaging carbon emissions this year. Carbon dioxide from oil, gas and coal is forecast to flatline for 2026, based on data from the year so far.
Last Thing: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists

blocks.caption: Tofane alpine skiing centre in Cortina. Photograph: Christophe Pallot/Agence Zoom/Getty Images

blocks.text: KFC will open its first high-altitude restaurants on the slopes of Cortina d’Ampezzo and Madonna di Campiglio, in the Dolomites. The move has not been entirely welcomed, with a prominent local businessman threatening legal action. The conflict hasn’t got quite as spicy yet as a recent food battle in Dortmund, however. Police were attacked as a crowd stormed a kebab shop that was offering introductory meals for the equivalent of $1.10.

articles.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian boy in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summary: The Israeli military says its soldiers opened fire at individuals “who intended to hurl stones” at a road used by Israelis.

blocks.text: Israeli forces have shot dead a 14-year-old Palestinian boy during an operation in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say.
Moataz Daghlas was killed on Monday evening in the village of Burqa, north-west of Nablus, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

The Israeli military said soldiers identified "several terrorists who intended to hurl stones" in an area where stones had previously been thrown at Israeli vehicles. The soldiers fired towards them "to remove the threat", it added.
The Palestinian Red Crescent said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds, but that Israeli forces blocked their access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.
Moataz Daghlas's relatives said Israeli authorities were withholding his body.

Meanwhile, Palestinian news agency Wafa identified the two Palestinians wounded during the raid as a 17-year-old child, who it said was shot in the abdomen and pelvis, and a 19-year-old man, who was shot in the hand.
According to the UN, at least 98 Palestinians, including 22 children, have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year.
Six Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians in the West Bank over the same period, it says.

The rules of engagement for Israeli forces were reportedly broadened after the deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023, allowing soldiers increased discretion to use lethal force against a perceived threat.

In June, the UN Human Rights Office in the occupied Palestinian territory said it had verified the killing of 241 Palestinian children by Israeli security forces and settlers in the West Bank since then.
Most of the children were teenage boys and, in many cases, Israeli authorities accused them of having engaged in stone-throwing as justification, it found.

The UN office said its assessment was that none of the children killed while involved in confrontations with Israeli forces had posed an imminent threat to life, which it said was the only legal justification for the use of lethal force in the West Bank under international law.

articles.title: Tiangco: Romualdez referred my additional budget request to Zaldy Co
articles.summary: Navotas Rep. Tobias Tiangco on Tuesday told the Sandiganbayan he approached Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez for additional funding for his district during Romualdez"s tenure as Speaker.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 7:22pm

Navotas Representative Tobias Tiangco on Tuesday told the Sandiganbayan he approached Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez for additional funding for his district during Romualdez’s tenure as Speaker.

Tiangco made the testimony during Romualdez's bail hearing at the Sandiganbayan Third Division, where the latter is facing a P7.4-billion plunder charge leveled against him and three others over their alleged links to the flood control mess.
Tiangco said Romualdez referred him to then-Ako Bicol party-list congressman Zaldy Co, who at the time was chair of the House appropriations committee.

Tiangco, however, said he did not reach out to Co. He said he learned from then-Pampanga congressman Aurelio "Dong" Gonzales Jr. that Co would ask for a 20% "taripa" or kickback, and that the kickback could even be lowered to 10% as “presyong kamag-anak” or friends and family rate.
Tiangco said he did not report the incident to Romualdez, but that the then-Speaker eventually called him in to discuss the issue.
“He [Romualdez] called me to meeting. Sabi ko, alam mo Speaker never ako lumapit sa iyo, pero since nagtatanong [ka] eto ang nangyari sa akin,” Tiangco said.
(I said, 'Speaker you know I didn't approach you about this, but since you're asking, this is what happened to me.)

Tiangco also reiterated his previous disclosures that President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr. scolded Romualdez and Co, with him present in a meeting, for refusing to fund the administration’s priority projects.
“I was embarrassed that the former Speaker was being scolded in front of me. It was after a family lunch in Bahay Pangulo. I was surprised,” he said.
Tiangco, however, clarified that Romualdez did not ask him for any taripa or commission and that he has no personal knowledge on supposedly deliveries on Romualdez.
Zaldy Co is facing multiple malversation, graft, and plunder cases and is currently at large.
Romualdez, meanwhile, is detained and has been suspended by the Sandiganbayan from performing his official duties for 90 days. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Defense did not coach witnesses -- Poa
articles.summary: The spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte"s defense team, Atty. Michael Poa, said they did not coach the witnesses they presented to the impeachment court.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 7:20pm
The spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team, Atty. Michael Poa, said they did not coach the witnesses they presented to the impeachment court.

On Tuesday, Duterte’s defense team presented Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan. The prosecution pointed out that Bajan had been a partner of the firm that audited companies linked to the Vice President.
Asked about these ties, Poa admitted that they did not know about these, as the defense did not “prep” the witnesses.

“We do not, to be very candid with you, when we call these witnesses, we needed them for specific purposes, but we do not prep them. Kung meron mang kaming communication whatsoever, it's just the scope. ” Poa said.
(We do not, to be very candid with you, when we call these witnesses, we needed them for specific purposes, but we do not prepare them. If there is communication whatsoever, it’s just the scope.)

“We don't really interview them muna, ‘di ba? Because we want them to be able to just state the facts as they are and we don't want to be accused of tampering with their testimonies or coaching them or anything like that. So yung sa mga ties, we did not know about that,” Poa added.

(We don’t really interview them first, right? Because we want them to be able to just state the facts as they are and we don't want to be accused of tampering with their testimonies or coaching them or anything like that. So these ties, we did not know about that.)
Poa also said he understood the frustrations of senator-judges, but said that there was a chance that the witnesses truly did not remember the answers to some of the questions directed at them.

“We would want our witnesses to be as straightforward as they can. Since they're under oath, kung hindi talaga nila natatandaan, mahirap naman sigurong gumawa din sila ng kwento kung hindi naman talaga nila natatandaan. But, we'll see,” Poa said.

(We would want our witnesses to be as straightforward as they can. Since they're under oath, if they really do not remember, it would be difficult to have them make up a story if they truly do not remember.)
Similar to defense witness Davao City Assessor Engineer Jaime Adalin, several senator-judges showed frustration with Bajan, with both seeming to forget details of matters that were asked of them.
Despite the frustrations of some senator-judges, Poa said that there was no need for the defense to shift their strategy. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
articles.summary: Felix Nmecha’s "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

image.caption: Felix Nmecha's 'Crowns down' celebration has sparked a response from Borussia Dortmund's fan clubImage: Madeleine Fantini/HMB Media/picture alliance

blocks.text: Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

"Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was launched.

"In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related issues and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.
"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent."

The fan club states their issue is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club said "gives us cause to reassess the situation."

This campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (BIG) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.
Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:
"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold."
Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.
Connections to US evangelical nonprofit in question

The fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends."

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's plan" and that homosexuality is a sin.

Borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone."

blocks.caption: Felix Nmecha first displayed the "Crowns down celebration" at the 2026 World CupImage: Christian Kolbert/kolbert-press/picture alliance

blocks.text: Law guarantees freedom to chose religion

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Big-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit."

And yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the new opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.
With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan orders 90-day suspension of Martin Romualdez
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the 90-day suspension of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, who is currently detained over a P7.4-billion plunder case.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 7:01pm
The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the 90-day suspension of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, who is currently detained over a P7.4-billion plunder case.
Sandiganbayan Third Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma confirmed the suspension order in a social media update by GMA News reporter Maki Pulido.
The resolution directs Romualdez, the incumbent Leyte 1st District representative, to cease and desist from performing his official functions for 90 days from receipt of the order.
“The court issued a resolution ordering the suspension pendente lite of former speaker Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez for a period of 90 days from receipt of the resolution,” Pulma told reporters.
The lawmaker's suspension pendente lite is a preventive measure while the criminal proceedings are ongoing.
“The resolution orders the former speaker to cease and desist from the functions of his office or any other office,” he added.
The anti-graft court also directed its clerk of court to furnish a copy of the resolution to the House Speaker through the Office of the Secretary General.
It further ordered the House to inform the court of any action taken within five days of receiving the resolution.

Romualdez is facing a plunder case over allegations that he and former Ako Bicol party-list representative Zaldy Co received at least P7.44 billion in kickbacks from contractors and other entities involved in government flood control, infrastructure and other projects from 2022 to 2025.

The Ombudsman alleged that the two lawmakers received commissions and other financial benefits in at least 15 transactions, with some of the proceeds supposedly laundered through shell corporations, financial intermediaries and property acquisitions.
Romualdez has denied the allegations and pleaded not guilty to the charge.
The former House Speaker was arrested on Sept. 7 at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City, where he was confined when authorities served the Sandiganbayan warrant.
He was transferred to the New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas on Sept. 14 following a medical assessment at the Philippine General Hospital.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Davao accountant can’t confirm own signature, tests senator-judges’ patience
articles.summary: The soft-spoken Vingelin Bajan elicits warnings of contempt as she evades questions on her former affiliation with the auditing firm that has among its clients Sara Duterte-linked companies, the Vice…

blocks.text: WITNESS. Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan during Day 41 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on November 10, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit

The soft-spoken Vingelin Bajan elicits warnings of contempt as she evades questions on her former affiliation with the auditing firm that has among its clients Sara Duterte-linked companies, the Vice President, and husband Mans Carpio

items: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte faced challenges as witnesses, including Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan, provided evasive answers, frustrating senator-judges.
Bajan's testimony raised concerns about her credibility, leading to calls from senator-judges for stricter adherence to court protocols and potential contempt citations.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

At the resumption of Vice President Sara Duterte‘s impeachment trial on Monday, November 9, senator-judges had to contend with what the prosecution called a “rude awakening” in the person of Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin, the defense witness who initially lied about a trip to China.

With that incident still fresh on the minds of senator-judges, two of them, Vicente “Tito” Sotto III and Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, on Tuesday, November 10, asked the impeachment court to remind witnesses of the penalties they face if they lie under oath. It was fair warning for all other witnesses of the trial, which Escudero would repeat every time a new witness took the stand.

Engineer John Kenneth Enumerables, city assessor of the Island Garden City of Samal, seemed to have heeded the reminder, and his testimony did not elicit any contempt warning. But then came the third defense witness, Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan.

At one point, the usually jovial presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero expressed frustration and said in a stern tone that his patience was “wearing thin” over Bajan’s “evasive” responses to the prosecution’s questions.
“My patience is wearing thin, forgive me,” Escudero told Bajan, as she directed her to respond to questions.

What was Bajan being evasive about? In challenging her credibility, House private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia asked the city accountant about her previous employment as a partner of the Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano, and Co. accounting firm.

Bajan repeatedly said she could not remember working as a partner of the firm. Confronted with documents bearing her own signatures, Bajan appeared confused, saying the Articles of Partnership and Amended Articles of Partnership, indeed, contained her tax account number and signatures similar to hers, but still could not recall signing them.
She was also seen looking at the defense team as she thought of what to say, which Divinagracia called out.
“I can’t recall all of these documents…. But this is my tax account number and signatures,” Bajan said.

Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano, and Co. — now Elises & Cuidadano — served as the external auditor of Gencorp Industries Incorporated and Metro City Chow Foods Inc., two companies linked to Duterte. Senator-judge Win Gatchalian said in his interjection later in the trial that the company is also the external auditor of the Vice President and her husband, Manases Carpio.

Frustration among the senator-judges was so strong that even Senator-judge Lito Lapid stood up to manifest what he thought about her testimony as well, saying: “Naawa na ako sa inyo. Kaming dalawa ni Sen Lacson…. Sa haba-haba nang halos maghapon na tanong ng mga senator-judge, halos hindi ‘nyo nasasagot.”
(I pity you. Both of us, Senator Lacson and I…. The senator-judges have been asking for hours and you hardly gave any answers.)
Bajan’s answers triggered senator-judges, who were already impatient following their experience with another Davao City official — Adalin — the past day.

“Yesterday, the witness was laughing and today, this witness is being evasive. Should we cite them in contempt to respect the impeachment court? Because as I see it, they have no respect for us,” said Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo.
“Maybe, it’s about that time we provide them as an example,” Tulfo added.
After being pressed by senator-judges, the city accountant admitted to being part of the firm. She likewise said she had forgotten leaving the firm in 2015.
However, Senator-judge Joel Villanueva countered her statement, emphasizing that the Amended Articles of Partnership included her signed affidavit of withdrawal.
“We’re practicing utmost patience with you. I hope you’ll help us help you,” said Villanueva.
The Senate impeachment court has repeatedly reminded witnesses against dodging questions during the trial.

Earlier in the day, Senator-judge Sotto inquired about the possible sanctions for witnesses lying under oath, with Senator-judge Lacson citing Senate Resolution No. 39, establishing the court’s contempt powers.

“Yesterday was not a good day for the impeachment court, Mr. President, Mr. Presiding Officer, simply because we had a witness who smirked, who laughed, almost made a mockery of the impeachment trial,” Lacson said.
“We don’t want to have a repeat of that kind of testimony,” he added.
Will the other witnesses finally heed the warning? – Rappler.com

articles.title: More than 250 mm of rain forecast for some B.C. areas as storm makes landfall
articles.summary: The B.C. River Forecast Centre has issued flood watches for the South Coast, Vancouver Island and river basins in the Central Coast and Fraser Valley.

image.caption: A person looks out onto the Canada Place seaplane terminal in Vancouver on Friday, when the first of a series of storms made landfall across southwest B.C. Another bout of heavy rain is forecast for some parts of B.C. Tuesday into Wednesday. (Ethan Cairns/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
The B.C. River Forecast Centre has issued flood watches for the South Coast, Vancouver Island and river basins in the Central Coast and Fraser Valley.
Number of storms led to thousands of people to lose power over weekend, with flood watches in place
A number of flood watches cover southwest B.C. as another storm system is set to impact the area on Tuesday, with forecasters predicting more than 250 millimetres of rain in some areas.
Thousands of British Columbians were battered by storms over the weekend, leading to numerous areas without power for multiple days as trees fell onto cars and power lines.

Though there was a slight reprieve in the rain for some areas on Monday, forecasters say they expect more rain on Tuesday and Wednesday, with more than 250 millimetres of rain possible locally, according to Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC).

"A very robust frontal system is set to make landfall on Vancouver Island very early Tuesday morning. Rain, heavy at times, will persist until Wednesday morning," reads an orange rainfall warning issued Monday for the west and central portions of the island.
"Even though the heaviest rain eases by Wednesday morning, moderate precipitation is expected to continue until Thursday morning."

Driver dead after tree hits car in Surrey as 2nd windstorm batters B.C.

blocks.text: In addition to the orange warning — which indicates widespread impacts — for much of Vancouver Island, yellow weather warnings are in place for Metro Vancouver's North Shore, Whistler and the Sunshine Coast.
ECCC is predicting 150 to 200 millimetres of rain for west and central Vancouver Island, and up to 120 millimetres of rain on the North Shore.

The #BC River Forecast Centre has UPGRADED to a Flood Watch for the South Coast (including #HoweSound, North Shore Mountains, #SeatoSky), Northern, Western, Central & East #VancouverIsland, the Central Coast (Kingcome & surrounding areas) & Fraser Valley-North. Avoid fast rivers & potentially unstable riverbanks. Never drive across flooded roads, bridges or river crossings. More info: https://t.co/W87tVOtUlp #BCFlood—EmergencyInfoBC
In the flood watch, the centre said that temperatures would be warm through Wednesday, which could mean snowmelt from shallow snowpacks at higher elevations.
"Heavy rain and high streamflow bring increased risk for unstable banks, river erosion, submerged roads, swift water hazards, flooding and landslides," the flood watch states.
"Stay clear of the banks of swift running rivers and never drive across flooded roads, bridges or river crossings."
Power outages
As of Monday night, thousands of B.C. Hydro customers — especially in the Central Interior and northern Vancouver Island — remained without power after the weekend storms.
The utility said that restoration efforts were continuing, even as it monitored the additional weather systems expected to move through B.C. in the coming days.

This is where a power line used to be. Reminder during #BCStorm: A downed, sagging, low-hanging or damaged power line is always an emergency. Stay back at least 10 metres (the length of a city bus) and call 911. Learn more: https://t.co/CEt5HXvd3F #CityofPG https://t.co/45MTitk5zT—bchydro
"Access remains a challenge in some areas, with fallen trees, debris and soft ground conditions slowing repair efforts," it said in a social media post.
Among the numerous areas in B.C. that have been without power for days is Zeballos on northwest Vancouver Island, where a number of properties are on evacuation order after a landslide last week.
Another storm expected for B.C. coast after wet, windy weekend
Road conditions
An orange rainfall warning is also in place for the Sea-to-Sky Highway, with ECCC saying up to 160 millimetres of rain is possible along the stretch and in the Howe Sound area.
A statement from the Road Safety at Work initiative recommended drivers check DriveBC for the latest updates and be prepared to drive for the conditions.
"You may not be able to see as far ahead, your tires have less grip, and you need more time and distance to stop safely," Trace Acres, a spokesperson for the initiative, said.

articles.title: [Local Vote] Voter registration for 2028: Answers to your common questions
articles.summary: The registration will run until July 30, 2027, Tuesdays to Fridays, 8 am to 5 pm

blocks.text: REGISTRATION. Cebu residents flock to the Commission on Elections office in Cebu City on November 10, 2026, as voter registration resumes for the 2028 national and local elections.
Jacqueline Hernandez/Rappler
The registration will run until July 30, 2027, Tuesdays to Fridays, 8 am to 5 pm

items: The voter registration for the 2028 elections in the Philippines reopened on November 10, 2026, and will close on July 30, 2027, with registration available from Tuesday to Friday and select Saturdays and holidays.

Eligible voters must be Filipino citizens, at least 18 years old by election day, and residents of the Philippines and their locality for specified durations, while certain individuals, such as those convicted of serious crimes, are disqualified from registering.
Various registration options are available, including local Comelec offices, satellite sites, and special programs, and applicants must provide identification documents or affidavits if they lack ID.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

The presidential, national, and local elections of 2028 are 18 months away, and prospective candidates will be filing their certificates in 11 months yet, but the poll season has technically started in the Philippines.
On Tuesday, November 10, the Commission on Elections (Comelec) resumed the registration of voters for the 2028 exercise.
So I guess I will also have to resume this early my Local Vote series, which I usually write only during campaign periods.
And for this edition, I have put together answers to your most common questions on voter registration. The answers are from various and relevant documents and information from the Comelec.

I will be updating this Q&A if and when there are new information you should know. In the meantime, you can also download Rappler’s MUNI app — for free — and join the Voter Hotline channel. There, we post updates about voter issues, while Comelec personnel and representatives of election watchdogs also address voter concerns.
The voter registration, which reopened on November 10, 2026, will close by end of day on July 30, 2027.
That’s a good eight months and 20 days, so I hope we can avoid any last-minute rush and, with it, the usually unfair criticism against the Comelec and its processes.
Registration days are from Tuesday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.
There will be Saturdays and holidays when the Comelec or its local offices can and will schedule registrations. Remember: not all Saturdays and holidays.

To know on which Saturdays and holidays registrations will be conducted, follow the Comelec’s official social media account or check with the election office in your city or municipality. Rappler’s Voter Hotline channel will also post advisories as they come in.

items: Local Comelec offices. They will accommodate you during office hours.
Comelec-approved satellite registration sites. These are usually malls or schools in key cities across the country. I will upload lists here once available.

Special Register Anytime/Anywhere Program (SRAP) sites. These are select areas where Comelec makes one-time deployments. For example: On November 10, the opening day of the voter registration period, a SRAP team was at the Mabini Hall in Luneta in Manila; it will be stationed there until Thursday, November. 12. It is open to the general public from 8 am to 6 pm. On November 19, SRAP will be at WalterMart Makati. It will also be open to the general public from 8 am to 5 pm. On November 24, a Comelec team will be at the Far Eastern University’s (FEU) Manila campus. The registration will be for FEU students only, from 8 am to 5 pm. You can check future SRAP locations and dates here.

blocks.caption: EARLY. Cebu City residents take advantage of the first voter registration day for the 2028 elections. Jacqueline Hernandez/Rappler

items: Filipino citizen
At least 18 years old by election day (May 8, 2028)
For at least one year before election day, a resident of the Philippines
For at least six months before election day, a resident of the locality where he/she intends to vote

Sentenced to prison for at least one year, unless pardoned or granted amnesty A person automatically reacquires his/her right to vote five years after serving his/her sentence. Reacquisition can happen earlier if his/her full civil and political rights are restored through plenary pardon or amnesty.

Convicted of rebellion, sedition, violation of the firearms laws, or any crime against national security A person automatically reacquires his/her right to vote five years after serving his/her sentence. Reacquisition can happen earlier if his/her full civil and political rights are restored in accordance with law.
Declared by a competent authority to be insane or incompetent, unless a proper authority declares the person is no longer suffering from such condition.
First-time voters
Voters who want to reactivate their records (after failing to vote for two consecutive elections)
Voters who want to transfer their registration within the locality (for example: from one barangay to another, or from one municipality to another)
Voters who want to correct certain entries in their records, or want to reflect changes in their names (for example: now carrying a spouse’s surname or marriage has been annulled)
Voters who want to transfer their records from a foreign service post to a local registration site
Persons with disabilities, senior citizens, members of Indigenous Peoples or Indigenous Cultural Communities, and other vulnerable sectors who need to update their records

Voters who will be abroad on election day. (These registrants can submit application forms online here, but they have to go to the Philippine embassy or consulate for the biometrics capturing. Once registered, they can only vote for national positions.)

blocks.caption: REGISTER ANYWHERE. First-time voters line up at the Comelec’s special registration site in Luneta Park in Manila on November 10, 2026 to register for the 2028 national and local elections. The registration period will run until July 30, 2027. Rappler photo

blocks.text: As of September 4, 2026, these are the deactivated voters. The Comelec has uploaded lists for every city and municipality. In every list, it is indicated whether the person failed to vote in two consecutive regular elections (totally deactivated and must register again) or has transferred and therefore has an active record in another city or municipality (so decide if you want to transfer to your old locality).

If your name is not on the list of deactivated voters, it means your registration is intact. So if you need to transfer or make changes to your record, go to your local Comelec office or to satellite registration sites.

items: Accomplished application form

Any of the following identification documents: National ID from PhilSys Postal ID card PWD ID Card Senior citizen’s ID card Student’s ID card or library card, signed by the school authority Driver’s license or student permit from the Land Transportation Office National Bureau of Investigation clearance Philippine passport Social Security System (SSS) or Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) or other Unified Multi-Purpose ID card Integrated Bar of the Philippines ID card License issued by the Professional Regulatory Commission Certificate of Confirmation issued by the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples Barangay Identification or certification with photo Any other government-issued valid IDs

blocks.text: If the applicant doesn’t have any of these IDs, in the absence of any of the above-mentioned identification documents, he/she can submit a sworn affidavit by any fourth-degree relative.

You don’t. The Comelec stopped issuing voter ID cards starting December 2017. This was after the House of Representative approved the bill seeking to establish a national identification system, under which a single ID would be issued to every citizen for all their government transactions.

(Republic Act 1105 or the Philippine Identification System Act was signed into law on August 6, 2018. We all know what happened to the national ID applications and issuance — many Filipinos are still waiting for their cards after years — but that’s a column for another day.)

Here’s a detail many people overlook: Submitting an application for registration doesn’t automatically make you a registered voter. Applications will be vetted and approved by an election registration board in every city and municipality. So far, these boards meet only once every 3 months, so they deliberate on the list per quarter — an incentive for you to register early. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Defense witness was partner at accounting firm for VP Sara business assets
articles.summary: A witness for the defense in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte used to be partner at the accounting firm for firms that are declared assets of Duterte and Mans Carpio.

blocks.text: A witness for the defense in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday was a partner at the accounting firm for companies that are declared assets of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.

Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia said that Davao City Accountant Vengeline Bahan used to be a partner at Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano & Co., CPAs, citing that her signature as partner is reflected in the firm’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) records, including the 2003 Articles of Partnership.
Divinangracia asked Bahan to confirm her signature as one of the firm’s partners based on SEC records, but Bahan could not give an answer.
"Pirma niyo ho yan, tama ba? Hindi niyo rin po ba makikilala ang inyong pirma?, Ms. Bahan, Divinagracia said.
(Can you confirm that this is your signature? Can you not recognize your signature?)
Bahan was still not giving any answer at this point and kept on flipping pages of the documents.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero cautioned Bahan against flipping pages, saying there is only one signature page.
Divinagracia responded by saying “We would just like to put it on record that this witness seems to refuse to answer or is hesitating to answer the question.”
Escudero then pressed Bahan to answer by asking if she is unfamiliar with the document.
Bahan answered in the affirmative.

When Divinagracia asked Bahan to confirm if Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano & Co., CPAs is the same accounting firm of GenCorp. Industries Inc., Metro City Chow Foods Corporation, Times Square B, City Hall King Chow, Chinese Gen B, Carpio Lawyers, Davao New Royal Taipan and Great Jolly Times Food Corporation as stated in these firms’ General Information Sheet (GIS) submitted to the SEC, Bahan said she could not recall such involvement of her former firm.
"You can refer to the General Information Sheets (GIS) to help you out,” Divinagracia said.
Defense counsel Lindon Bacquel objected to the question, but this was overruled by Escudero.
Bahan responded, “Hindi ko po ma-remember.” (I cannot recall.)

Bahan, however, confirmed that Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano & Co., CPAs original Articles of Partnership dated 2003 and amended Articles of Partnership in 2015, there is only one SEC registration number for the said firm.
“Pareho po [ang SEC registration] number,” Bahan said.
Escudero then asked Bahan if she ever served as external accountant of Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano & Co., CPAs, to which Bahan replied, “Hindi ko po ma-remember your honor, sa tagal na po.”
(I cannot remember, your honor. It has been too long.)

Bahan, however, confirmed that she was a partner of the accounting firm Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano & Co., CPAs and left the firm in 2015 when she was confronted by the same documents, including her affidavit of withdrawal as firm’s partner in 2015, by Senator-judge Joel Villanueva.
Villanueva read a portion of Bahan’s affidavit which read “I resigned in the partnership effective August 1, 2015 due to personal reasons."
“Sigurado po ako ito ang pirma niyo dahil ito ang nasa official record,” Villanueva said.
“Para sabihin niyo na hindi niyo maalala, mahirap ho kami makumbinsi sa ganun. You are not contesting this [affidavit of withdrawal]?,” Villanueva added.
Bahan answered in the affirmative. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: U.S. request for Quiboloy extradition reaches Makati court
articles.summary: The case seeking his surrender to the US was filed before a Makati court.

blocks.text: November 10, 2026 | 6:47pm
Kingdom of Jesus Christ leader Apollo Quiboloy faces the Senate at a hearing on religious human trafficking in October 2024.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed a petition before a Makati court seeking the extradition of Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Apollo Quiboloy and two others to the United States.

In a press briefer sent to reporters on Tuesday, November 10, the DOJ said the extradition petition against Quiboloy, Teresita Tolibas Dandan and Helen Panilag was filed before Makati Regional Trial Court Branch 145 on November 9.

The DOJ explained that under the rules governing extradition proceedings, the court may issue an arrest warrant against the respondents, while the clerk of court is tasked with issuing summons to be served personally along with the petition and its accompanying documents.
The U.S. case against Quiboloy includes:

items: international human trafficking,
sex trafficking,
conspiracy, and
bulk cash smuggling

blocks.text: The justice department said extradition proceedings do not determine the criminal liability of the respondents.

"An extradition proceeding is sui generis. It is not a criminal proceeding and it does not involve the determination of the guilt or innocence of an accused. His guilt or innocence will be adjudged in the court of the state where he will be extradited," the DOJ said.
Quiboloy was indicted by a US federal grand jury in 2021 on charges that include conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion and sex trafficking of children.
U.S. prosecutors have accused Quiboloy and other Kingdom of Jesus Christ officials of recruiting women and girls as personal assistants and coercing them into sex.
Quiboloy has denied the allegations.
In the Philippines, he remains detained while facing child and sexual abuse cases before a Quezon City court and a qualified human trafficking case before a Pasig court.

articles.title: Jinggoy Estrada had P1.6 billion in budget insertions, says witness
articles.summary: Senator Jinggoy Estrada inserted over P1.6 billion worth of projects in the budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) in 2025, a witness told the Sandiganbayan on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 6:46pm
Senator Jinggoy Estrada inserted over P1.6 billion worth of projects in the budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) in 2025, a witness told the Sandiganbayan on Tuesday.
According to the judicial affidavit of witness DPWH Programming Division Chief Engr. Peter Paul Cortez, these budget insertions were spread across 16 projects.

Testifying before the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division, Cortez said that these insertions were in the 1st and 3rd District Engineering Offices of Bulacan. He also alleged that there were budget insertions at the National Capital Region office.
The DPWH employee also said that these projects appeared in the 2025 General Appropriations Act (GAA) without appearing in the National Expenditure Program.
Cortez reportedly found out about Estrada’s projects because this was part of the list given to him by the late DPWH undersecretary Catalina Cabral.
Cabral reportedly sent the list to his office so that it could be encoded into the DPWH’s database.
Estrada is currently being tried for a P573 million plunder case in relation to the flood control scam.

Billions of pesos were allegedly funneled through bogus flood control projects, with officials and lawmakers allegedly pocketing millions in the process. Estrada is among those who have been accused of being part of the scam. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Davao City accountant Bajan admits going to China in December 2025
articles.summary: Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan, a witness presented by the defense in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, confirmed Tuesday that she was one of the local officials who…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 6:37pm

Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan, a witness presented by the defense in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, confirmed Tuesday that she was one of the local officials who traveled to China late last year.
Bajan confirmed this during her cross examination by private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia on the 41st day of the trial.
"First week po ng December (It was on the first week of December)," the witness said.
Divinagracia then asked her if the galunggong from China tastes better.
"Mas mura po (It's cheaper)," Bajan answered.
The private prosecutor also asked Bajan if she knew that other Davao City officials also went to China in January this year.
"Hindi ko po alam kasi 'yung akin lang po ang alam ko," the witness said.
(I don't know, because I only know about my own trip.)
However, she clarified that the trip to China with her friends was "personal" and was arranged as a "reward" for herself and her companions.
"Kami po [nagbayad], Your Honor. Parang every ano kasi… parang reward sa amin po. Nagbiyahe po kami," Bajan said, during the interjection of Senator-Judge Risa Hontiveros.
(We paid for it ourselves, Your Honor. It was sort of a reward for ourselves, so we went on a trip.)
"Rewards po sa sarili po namin po. Parang sa ka-busy busy po ng trabaho at isa po sa bucket list ko po ang makita ko po yung Shanghai at Beijing," she added.
(It was a reward for ourselves. Given how busy work has been and visiting Shanghai and Beijing was actually on my bucket list.)
Bajan also said nobody invited their group to go to China and they only arranged their itinerary themselves.
Hontiveros then asked the witness to submit to the impeachment court a copy of her travel authority to China.
On Monday, Davao City assessor Engineer Jaime Adalin, the first witness presented by the defense, was grilled by the prosecution and some senator-judges about his travel to China.

During his cross-examination, Adalin said he could not remember details of the trip, but he later admitted going to China in January 2026 for "personal" travel, following repeated questions by senator-judges. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Brand barrister’s cross-examination of victims shocking and depressing, says Labour deputy
articles.summary: Lucy Powell says she thought ‘we’d gone past that sort of culture’, and that she regrets setting up Miliband interview with comedian in 2015

blocks.text: Labour’s deputy leader, Lucy Powell, has criticised the “depressing” nature of the cross-examination of Russell Brand’s victims during his trial for rape and sexual assault, saying she believed the courts had “long gone past that sort of culture”.
Powell, now the education secretary, also said she regretted the meeting that the former party leader Ed Miliband had with Brand in 2015, when she was Labour’s campaign chief.
Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years on Monday for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others, including at their workplaces.

Powell was asked on LBC radio about Brand’s defence in court, during which his barrister, Ian Winter KC, suggested Brand must be innocent because none of his victims had “resisted or screamed or even tried to leave”. Winter also said the anal rape of a 21-year-old woman by Brand was a “short and momentary failure” where “he did not respect her consent”.

blocks.caption: Ian Winter KC leaving Southwark crown court after Brand was sentenced to 10 and a half years in prison. Photograph: Tayfun Salci

blocks.text: Asked if that was reminiscent of the attitude of the 1950s, Powell said she had been “shocked” at some of what took place in the courtroom, while praising the judge’s words. “I found reading some of that incredibly sort of depressing. I thought we’d long gone past that sort of culture and that phase of things.

“And the judge’s remarks were also incredibly powerful in sentencing: that it doesn’t matter what you wear, how you behaved, how drunk you are, you know, you have the right to give your consent or not give your consent. And if it’s not given, then that is rape and that is a sexual offence, pure and simple.”

Powell said the government had taken steps in guidance to challenge myths around rape and victim-blaming. “But clearly, a lot more needs to be done because I think many of us were really shocked that that could still take place in a courtroom today,” she said.
At sentencing, the judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, criticised Brand, saying the women had been subjected to additional suffering because of the conduct in court “on your instructions”.

“Whatever women wear, wherever they go, whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and demand justice in the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Mr Brand, act without their consent,” he said.

Powell said she and Miliband regretted that he had done an interview with Brand in 2015 during the hype around Revolution, Brand’s book on politics. At the time the interview took place, Brand had resigned his BBC Radio 2 show for leaving a series of lewd messages on actor Andrew Sachs’ answerphone about his granddaughter.
after newsletter promotion

“It was a long time ago, obviously, and had I or Ed Miliband or anybody at the time had any sense at all that this was someone who was a sexual predator, who was involved in these sorts of crimes,” she told Sky News, anyone who was involved in promoting him would “look back and really regret that, knowing today what we now know”.

Asked about her role in setting up the interview, Powell said she had not understood the full extent of his sexual conduct that was already in the public domain – such as in his autobiography. “If there was any suggestion at all we were dealing with someone who was a known sexual predator at the time then, of course, no one would have done that.
“But as I say, he was a well-known public figure. Lots of people, from Hollywood to the BBC to many others, gave this person a very, very powerful platform.”

articles.summary: 'The court issued a resolution ordering the suspension pendente lite of former speaker Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez for a period of 90 days from receipt of the resolution,' says the Sandiganbayan…

blocks.text: ARRAIGNMENT. Former House speaker Martin Romualdez during his arraignment on September 16, 2026.
Aaron Favila/AP/Sandiganbayan pool

'The court issued a resolution ordering the suspension pendente lite of former speaker Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez for a period of 90 days from receipt of the resolution,' says the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division
MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan 3rd Division ordered the suspension of former speaker Martin Romualdez due to his plunder case related to the flood control scandal.

“The court issued a resolution ordering the suspension pendente lite of former speaker Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez for a period of 90 days from receipt of the resolution. The resolution orders the former speaker to cease and desist from the functions of his office or any other office,” 3rd Division Executive Clerk Dennis Pulma said on Tuesday, November 10.
Romualdez is facing plunder, a non-bailable offense, due to alleged P7.44-billion in kickbacks from government projects.

The Office of the Ombudsman filed the plunder charge against him with the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan on September 7. On the same day, the 3rd Division issued a warrant of arrest against Romualdez and ordered his detention.
The lawmaker, a first cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., has been detained in the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas since September 14.

Under Section 5 of Republic Act No. 7080 or the Plunder Law, any public officer charged with the case “whatever stage of execution and mode of participation, is pending in court, shall be suspended from office.”
Romualdez is Leyte 1st District representative – Rappler.com

articles.title: David Jones’s finances were reviewed and restructuring flagged months before it fell into administration
articles.summary:
Department store group kept buying new products and fell months behind in payments to some brands despite discussions with administrators

  • Get our

blocks.text: David Jones’s administrators have revealed they reviewed its finances six months ago and discussed restructuring the retailer three months before it fell into administration.

The new timeline raises questions over the department store group’s decision to keep buying new products and fall months behind in payments to some brands before it revealed last Thursday it could not pay its debts.
The process could leave unsecured creditors with substantial losses, with unpaid product suppliers and shoppers holding unredeemed gift vouchers most at risk.
The McGrathNicol administrators invited David Jones’s creditors, which also include employees and landlords, to attend a 17 November meeting in its first circular on Tuesday.

McGrathNicol’s team said it had been engaged by the lawyers for David Jones’s owners, Anchorage Capital, as early as April 2026 to analyse some of the department store group’s financial information, though it said it did not directly advise the group or review its ability to pay debts.

By July, David Jones’s group director, Simon Woodhouse, and its biggest lender, Hilco, met McGrathNicol to discuss David Jones’s financial performance, “potential restructuring” and to form a working group to regularly discuss the issues.
But the administrators said Woodhouse left the meeting when the “potential restructuring” was discussed and no working group was formed.

At the same time, David Jones was putting small suppliers on tiered and extended payment terms, with brands forced to accept ever-deeper discounts to get faster payments, according to several businesses contacted by Guardian Australia.
McGrathNicol said it did not discuss David Jones’s dire financial position again until 22 October, when Woodhouse asked them to help plan a for potential voluntary administration.

It said Woodhouse and others held another five meetings in the following fortnight before a series of briefings last Wednesday, the day before the administration was announced, as the company negotiated with its landlords and prepared for collapse.
McGrathNicol said David Jones Group paid it $1m upfront that day to run the administration. It told creditors it expected to access another $3m to $4m of funding.
The first creditors’ meeting will take place on 17 November, McGrathNicol said.

A second meeting is typically required six weeks later but McGrathNicol said it would apply to have that delayed another three months, or to early April 2027, to give it more time to sell the business or raise more funds.

The letter did not offer more detail on David Jones’s financial situation, or how long it had been insolvent. McGrathNicol said it had asked the company’s directors to prepare a report on their business, property and financial circumstances.
FTI Consulting, which is running David Jones’s day-to-day business during the administration process, on Monday said the company had remained fully operational.
Anchorage Capital, David Jones and Hilco were contacted for comment on Tuesday night.
